newsitem.title: USA: CSX, Norfolk Southern see Conrail plan filed soon.
newsitem.headline: CSX, Norfolk Southern see Conrail plan filed soon.

text.p: Railroads CSX Corp. and Norfolk Southern Corp. said Tuesday they plan to file their plan for the proposed $10.3 billion acquisition of Conrail Inc. with federal regulators in several days.

The filing had been expected on Monday or Tuesday of this week but has been delayed due to the complexity of the document, which contains more than 15,000 pages, the two prospective buyers said in a joint statement.

Sources familiar with the plan told Reuters there were no other reasons for the delay and the proposed transaction was not in jeopardy. The companies said they will make a public announcement as soon as the application is filed.

CSX, based in Richmond, Va., and Norfolk Southern, based in Norfolk, Va., are seeking approval to buy the East Coast railroad and then divide the assets. The deal calls for Norfolk to pay $5.9 billion for 58 percent of Conrail and CSX to pay $4.3 billion for the rest.

The plan, to be submitted to the Surface Transportation Board, the federal agency that oversees railroads, is expected to contain details about capital expenditures, cost savings and other key aspects of the transaction.
CSX stock fell $1 to $53.75 and Norfolk Southern fell $1 to $99.50, both in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
